Hi Oliver —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and the recommended next steps so we have a mutual action plan: 

Summary of ask:
- Ingest / extraction work on semi-structured documents (~2k tokens typical, spikes to 10k)
- Tight p95 latency target (~250ms) for user-facing autocomplete use-case
- High throughput during nightly batch re-ranking (10s TPS target)

Recommended initial model candidates (based on today's workload notes):
- redwood-3b-int8: strong cost/latency tradeoff for online autocomplete (good p50/p90)
- redwood-7b-qat: better quality with quantized weights; expect higher p95 but superior hallucination profile on our eval sets
- open-flan-xxl-quant (v2): solid for nightly re-ranks where throughput > strict latency

What I'll share after this email:
- Redwood-verified performance profiles (CSV) showing TPS and latency percentiles across batch sizes
- The exact prompt set we used for your eval (attached) and the short prompt tuning notes
- Links to the console benchmark run for the configurations I mentioned

Next steps proposed:
1) We’ll drop the attached prompt set into your evaluation harness and re-run with the two suggested models (redwood-3b-int8, redwood-7b-qat). (Owner: Rishi / Marissa)
2) Marissa will share the Redwood-verified profiles and a short summary of p95/p99 behavior for each model at batch sizes 1/4/8. (Owner: Marissa)
3) Schedule a 30-min follow-up to review quality regressions and SLA implications — suggest Wed 05/05 or Thu 05/06.

Attachments: redwood_verified_profiles_20270503.csv, acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl

If this looks right, I’ll queue the benchmark runs and put the follow-up on your calendar.

Thanks,
Rishi

Hi Oliver — following up with the concrete numbers from our Redwood-verified runs. I’ve attached the CSV (redwood_verified_profiles_20270503.csv) and pasted the short summary below. The CSV includes per-model runs across batch sizes 1, 4, 8 on an nvidia-a100-80gb equivalent profile we used for parity testing.

Quick perf summary (median of multiple runs):
- redwood-3b-int8 (batch=1): TPS ~ 12, p50 28ms, p90 110ms, p95 210ms, p99 370ms
- redwood-3b-int8 (batch=4): TPS ~ 38, p50 34ms, p90 130ms, p95 240ms, p99 420ms
- redwood-7b-qat (batch=1): TPS ~ 6, p50 45ms, p90 160ms, p95 300ms, p99 560ms
- open-flan-xxl-quant (batch=8): TPS ~ 22, p50 120ms, p90 420ms, p95 760ms

Quality notes from the eval prompt set (attached acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl):
- redwood-3b-int8: highest cost/latency efficiency, low token-level hallucinations on extraction prompts but occasional context-window truncation on 10k token spikes; performs well with short instruction priming (see prompt example 2).
- redwood-7b-qat: lower hallucination rate on open-ended QAs in our prompt set; better at multi-step reasoning prompts but at the cost of higher p95 latency.
- open-flan-xxl-quant: best for reranking and high-throughput re-scoring; quality is strong on ranking metrics but response generation is heavier.

Suggested first-pass prompt engineering (keeps changes minimal):
1) Use explicit system instruction: "System: You are a structured-extraction assistant. Always return JSON with keys: entity, value, confidence."
2) Provide 2-shot positive examples for tricky fields in the same prompt payload rather than relying on completions-only context.
3) Enforce token caps for user-facing autocomplete paths (truncate to the most recent 2k tokens) to avoid long-context p95 spikes.

Operational notes:
- For strict p95 <= 250ms at batch=1, redwood-3b-int8 is borderline but achievable with the A100 profile — we saw p95 ~210ms in our runs. If you need headroom, either accept a small fraction of traffic routed to a faster dedicated instance or move to the 7b-qat and budget for higher latency.
- We recommend running a 24-hour soak with your spike profile before committing to a Reserved/Dedicated proposal — this will surface tail behaviors.

Benchmarks and links: 
- Console run: https://console.redwood.ai/benchmarks/DEAL-2027-0142
- CSV (attached): redwood_verified_profiles_20270503.csv
- Prompt set (attached): acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl

I’m happy to run the batch jobs on our side and share raw logs (if you prefer we can also give a read-only console link). Rishi — if we agree, I’ll spin up the 3b-int8 run in hosted first, then push to their dev cluster config.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
